_label: The distillation of the completed ModelLake march. Read this before specimen 46.
_evidence: Every claim traces to a committed receipt under receipts/odyssey-i/. Nothing here is new measurement; it is what the measurements collectively mean.
census_status: COMPLETE -- 53 distinct specimens carry a real measurement; 0 remain classification-only; 2 resist static measurement entirely (evo2_40b split .pt, mamba3-mimo .bin) and are recorded as such rather than skipped.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: MEASURE THE BODY, NEVER THE NAME.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: five independent name-vs-measurement gaps: BitNet ships 2.0 bits/weight against its own '1.58' name; pi0's action expert measures 575M against a 'gemma_300m' label; iLLaDA's raw params are 8.28% over its README until a duplicated tied tensor is removed; Qwen3-0.6B is 25.27% over its name for the same reason; Mistral-Small-24B measures 48B until you notice it ships the same model twice.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: never quote a nameplate as a measurement, and when a measurement disagrees with a name, find the mechanism before publishing either.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: AN EXACT FACTOR OF TWO IS A COUNTING BUG UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: Mistral-Small-3.1-24B measured 48.02B against a 24B name. Four genuine name-vs-measurement findings already existed, so a fifth looked plausible. It was a glob counting consolidated.safetensors AND its 10-shard twin: 585 tensors each, zero name overlap, identical shape/dtype multisets.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: prefer shards, never sum a consolidated copy alongside them, and treat suspiciously round ratios as arithmetic before treating them as discoveries.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: A CONFIG FLAG PREDICTS NOTHING; ONLY BYTES SETTLE IT.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: R-tied-embedding-dedup-verify across 8 specimens: 2 wasteful, 4 clean, 2 untied. Settled by a within-vendor counter-example -- Qwen3-0.6B duplicates its tied matrix while Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B does not, same lab, same 0.6B class, same model_type -- which forecloses family, format and scale as explanations. Also Dream-v0's use_cache=true, which its own generation loop ignores.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: verify declared properties at the byte level. The rule's entire value is its verify step.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: HETEROGENEITY IN A CONFIG IS NOT NECESSARILY HETEROGENEITY IN THE WEIGHTS.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: ModernBERT-large alternates local and global attention every 3rd layer, and those layers are BYTE-IDENTICALLY structured -- the alternation is a runtime mask policy costing zero stored bytes. LFM2-24B's conv-vs-attention heterogeneity IS paid for in weights.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: before keying an allocation rule on 'layer type', check whether the types differ in tensors.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: SPECIALIST BODIES HAVE EXACTLY ONE ORGAN WORTH ATTACKING.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: Depth-Anything backbone 90.8%, SmolVLM2 model 95.5%, sam2.1 vision_encoder 94.8%, vjepa2 encoder 97.8%, timesfm decoder 99.0%.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: on a non-language-decoder body, every MoE-derived allocation lever has no surface. The search is 'compress the backbone or achieve nothing' -- narrower and harder, and worth planning as such rather than discovering by trying rules that cannot apply.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: THE GATHER LEVER IS BOUNDED BY SHARED MASS, NOT BY THE TOP-K RATIO.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: R-sparse-active-expert-gather transferred on 10 of 12 MoE bodies and failed on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next -- which has the SPARSEST routing in the population (10 of 512) and still runs 32.8% active, because 31.5% of it is non-expert mass. Refined law active = non_expert + expert*(k/E) reproduces the measurement to 0.04pp.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: measure expert_mass/total before funding a gather implementation. Its ceiling is 1 - non_expert_fraction.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: ADVERTISED CONTEXT IS A MEMORY LIABILITY, NOT ONLY A CAPABILITY.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: KV at full advertised context exceeds model weights for several Resident candidates (Qwen3-4B: 36.0 GiB KV against 7.5 GiB of weights). Olmo-3-7B has no GQA at all -- 512 KiB/token, 8x the cheapest candidate -- and nothing in its parameter count reveals it.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: the memory denominator is weights + KV at the context actually used. Compute it from layers x kv_heads x head_dim, never from parameter count.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: SIZE DOES NOT GATE STATIC ANALYSIS. ONLY EXECUTION IS GATED.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: the frontier tier sat unexamined for the whole campaign as though 1.45TB were prohibitive. A safetensors header is a length prefix plus JSON at the head of each shard: Kimi-K3 yielded 1503.65B params / 83.02B active / 1.04 bytes-per-param for the same cost as a 3GB body.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: never defer a header read for size. Defer only what needs the GPU.

LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.law: SET THE EBPW BASELINE FROM THE REAL DTYPE MIX.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.earned_from: Kimi-K3 1.04, GLM-5.3-Flash 1.02 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash 1.01 bytes/param -- already sub-bf16 at rest (F8_E4M3, F8_E8M0 scales, I8 payloads). BitNet's complete-system EBPW is 3.91 despite 86% of its params being 2-bit ternary, because embeddings and norms stay BF16.
LAWS_THAT_MAKE_THE_NEXT_MODEL_CHEAPER.use: comparing a Gravity result against an assumed fp16 parent overstates the win on any of these. Always keep the complete system in the denominator.

METHOD_TRAPS_CAUGHT_THIS_MARCH: A dtype missing from the table silently defaults and inflates a total -- F8_E8M0 cost DeepSeek-V4 8GiB of phantom size until the table was completed.
'Unmeasurable' often means 'the glob did not look' -- audio-flamingo-3 keeps tensors under llm/ + sound_tower/, Wan2.2-T2V under high_noise_model/. Recursive lookup measured both.
Checking a sample and generalising: LFM2-24B looked like 'conv layers dense, attention layers MoE' from layers 0 and 2. All 40 checked: only layers 0-1 are dense, by absolute position.
A hand-eyeballed count is not a count -- RWKV7's layer 0 carries 2 extra tensors the other 60 do not.
A family name is not a structure -- LFM2.5 keeps the conv+attention split and drops the MoE entirely, so a rule keyed on 'LFM2' would find no expert organ and silently do nothing.
A rulebase entry authored in a different schema breaks every consumer that iterates it -- the A5 rule used title/claim where twelve others use conditions/then, and was found by exactly that crash.
WHAT_REMAINS_GATED: EXECUTION, and only execution. No capability battery, Gravity codec search, NR/Noetic/NX build or physical run has happened for any specimen, because all of those need the GPU the HCLI resident holds. Every static question the march could answer has been answered.
RANKED_CONTINUATION_WHEN_GPU_OPENS: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B -- the only Resident candidate that is MoE, code-specialised and long-context at once, and the natural next Gravity patient after O005/O006 since the expert-organ rules apply directly.
Kimi-K3 / GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V4-Flash -- frontier MoE with expert mass above 90% and already sub-bf16, so the gather lever is nearly the whole battle and the EBPW baseline is unusual.
Dream-v0 and iLLaDA -- the steps-vs-quality tradeoff is the efficiency question for masked-diffusion LMs and has no analogue in any other family surveyed.
LFM2.5-2.6B -- cheapest long context measured (60 KiB/token, 8 of 30 layers attention), the clearest test of whether A5's hybrid-ratio rule predicts real served memory.
